title: Why your Pod's IP address is a trap
caption: Kubernetes Services explained simply. Do you use ClusterIP, NodePort, or LoadBalancer the most?

scenes.vo: Pods die all the time, and every new Pod gets a completely different IP. How do clients ever find your app?
scenes.heading: SERVICE

scenes.vo: When a backend Pod crashes, Kubernetes replaces it instantly. But its IP address vanishes into thin air.
scenes.heading: DYNAMIC IPS

scenes.vo: A Service acts like a company switchboard. Callers dial one permanent number, and the operator routes them to anyone sitting at their desk.
scenes.heading: THE SWITCHBOARD
scenes.line: One number forwarding to available desks

scenes.vo: Traffic hits one stable virtual IP. The Service automatically balances requests across all healthy Pods using labels.
scenes.heading: HOW IT WORKS

scenes.vo: Never wire hardcoded IPs. Just run kubectl expose to create a load-balanced Service in one line.
scenes.heading: THE TRICK

scenes.vo: Services provide a stable IP, internal load balancing, and label-based discovery. Follow for more simple Kubernetes!
scenes.heading: SERVICE
